notes: On the basis of actual Police strength (Civil + Armed), the comparative rate of complaints per 100 Policemen is
computed for each State/UT and is presented in Table-16(D). Among the States, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand reported
48.6 and 16.8 complaints per 100 Policemen respectively. Complaints per 100 Policemen reported in Delhi was 17.6
against the national average of 3.3 during the year 2002. Table-17.5 (Chapter-17) reflects low Police strength (38 per
lakh population) in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh (57 per lakh population) compared to the National average of 125 and
Delhi (381). This could be attributed to the higher rate of complaints against Police in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand
Since 1999, an attempt has been made to gather information on details of cases where human rights were violated
due to Police excesses such as `Illegal Detentions’, `Fake Encounters’, `Extortion’, `Torture’, etc. The details are
During the year, 95 cases of Human Rights Violation by Police were reported throughout the country. For these
Human Rights Violation, 59 Policemen were charge-sheeted but none of them was convicted. Andhra Pradesh reported
the maximum 26 (27.4%) of such cases followed by Gujarat 14 (14.7%). No case was reported from any of the UTs.
Out of the 95 cases, 14 were reported for `Atrocities on SC/ST’, 10 for `Indignity to Women’ 4 for `Extortion’, 9 for
`Illegal Detention/Arrests’, 5 for `Disappearance of Persons’ and 3 for `Torture’ etc.
